title: Pluralistic Alignment in Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model response probability distributions against empirical survey data from specific demographic subgroups (e.g., age, gender, race/ethnicity, religion) using metrics like Jensen-Shannon divergence and Total Variation distance to measure representational fidelity and prevent minority viewpoint suppression.

Evaluating model responses against country-specific and regional survey distributions (e.g., GlobalOpinionQA) to diagnose 'cultural flattening' (compressing differences between countries) and 'caricature' (exaggerating differences not supported by respondents).

Measuring 'Overton Pluralism' by assessing whether a model generates and covers a valid, human-supported set of diverse viewpoints on contested social or political issues, rather than collapsing responses into a single default consensus.
